title: Insulin Pump Program Financial Assistance Computation Sheet: Hardship Waiver Amount
content:
A hardship waiver on an Insulin Pump Program is posted against the posting the program's approved hardship application names, for the amount worked out as follows.

**Waiver base.** The waiver base is the named posting's amount less every balance adjustment already posted against it, never below zero. For a hardship waiver, and only for such a waiver, the waiver is figured on the named posting's amount less the adjustments against it even where payments were already applied to that posting, and any payment it leaves uncovered is applied to the program's next oldest unpaid posting or refunded under the credit-balance rule, as financial assistance refunds what a customer paid above the assisted amount; a billing correction follows its own limit, and every other adjustment keeps the general unpaid-remainder limit.

**Standard computation.** In the standard computation the waiver is the standard share percent of 40 percent of the waiver base, rounded half up to the cent.

**Combination.** Any adjustment to the standard share changes it as that adjustment states, a replacement taking precedence over additions; the share is never more than 100 percent, and the waiver is the waiver base times the share, rounded half up to the cent.

## Standard computation worked through (hypothetical postings)

| Named posting | Adjustments already against it | Payments applied to it | Waiver base | Waiver at 40 percent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $180.00 | none | none | $180.00 | $72.00 |
| $180.00 | $20.00 | $50.00 | $160.00 (payments do not reduce the base) | $64.00 |
| $85.25 | none | none | $85.25 | $34.10 |
| $40.00 | $45.00 | none | $0.00 (never below zero) | $0.00 |

In the second row the $50.00 already paid against the posting is not deducted from the base; any payment the waiver leaves uncovered is applied to the program's next oldest unpaid posting or refunded under the credit-balance rule.
